title: 9 Oct 2026 (Khobar)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Khobar, 9 October 2026 (handwritten notes, some pages missing)

questions.question: A newborn has a skin-covered sac protruding through a skull defect at the occiput. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Neural tube defect of the skull.

questions.question: A newborn has abdominal contents covered by a membrane protruding through the umbilical ring. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Omphalocele has a sac and associated anomalies (trisomies, Beckwith-Wiedemann); gastroschisis has no sac and lies right of the cord.

questions.question: An infant has a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 280/min with no visible P waves. What is the rhythm?
questions.exp: SVT rate is usually > 220 in infants, with fixed RR intervals.

questions.question: A child has wide splitting of S2 and a murmur at the left 2nd intercostal space. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pulmonary flow murmur with fixed wide split S2.

questions.question: A short child (height 115 cm, elfin facies) has an ejection systolic murmur. What is the lesion?
questions.exp: Williams syndrome.

questions.question: A child has normocytic anaemia, raised reticulocytes, raised bilirubin and splenomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Haemolysis with spherocytes, raised MCHC and family history.

questions.question: A child has fever for 2 weeks, a grade 4 murmur, bone pain, liver 2 cm and spleen 1 cm palpable. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Prolonged fever with splenomegaly favours endocarditis. The recall writer chose endocarditis.

questions.question: An ABG shows pH 7.25, high PaCO2 and low PaO2. What is the interpretation?
questions.exp: Hypoventilation. Exact values were not recorded.

questions.question: A child with ataxia has recurrent chest infections and deteriorating pneumonia. What treatment reduces infections?
questions.exp: Ataxia telangiectasia with antibody deficiency benefits from IVIG and antibiotic prophylaxis.

questions.question: A child with recurrent watery diarrhoea since birth is admitted with low serum chloride and metabolic alkalosis. What is the most useful test?
questions.exp: Congenital chloride diarrhoea has stool chloride > 90 mmol/L with low urine chloride. The recall writer chose urine chloride.

questions.question: Which acid-base disturbance is common in cystic fibrosis?
questions.exp: Salt loss in sweat.

questions.question: What is the commonest neonatal presentation of cystic fibrosis?
questions.exp: Meconium ileus occurs in 15-20% of CF newborns.

questions.question: A doctor is about to examine a crying child. What is the first action?
questions.exp: Hand hygiene before patient contact.
questions.c: Ask the mother to hold him

questions.question: Which method removes the greatest number of organisms from the hands?
questions.exp: Antiseptic hand rub removes more organisms than a short wash.

questions.question: What is a common presentation of hypervitaminosis D?
questions.exp: Hypercalcaemia causes polyuria, polydipsia, vomiting and later nephrocalcinosis. The recall writer chose stones but noted polyuria.

questions.question: A child with sarcoidosis needs treatment for progressive disease. What is used?
questions.exp: Steroids are first-line; methotrexate spares steroids.
questions.d: Prednisolone, with methotrexate as a steroid-sparing agent

questions.question: Which condition causes a false negative sweat chloride test?
questions.exp: Oedema lowers sweat chloride.

questions.question: A 3-year-old has severe epigastric pain and tenderness, and X-ray shows a coin-shaped radio-opacity in the epigastrium. What is the management?
questions.exp: A symptomatic disc-shaped object may be a button battery. The recall writer considered pancreatic calcification.
questions.b: Upper GI endoscopy (exclude a button battery)

questions.question: A 5-year-old has cough, dyspnoea and dullness, with a dense lobar opacity on X-ray. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dullness with lobar consolidation.

questions.question: A child stung by a scorpion cannot see well. Which sign is expected?
questions.exp: Adrenergic storm with tachycardia, sweating and hypersalivation.

questions.question: Which investigation is useful after a scorpion sting?
questions.exp: The recall writer chose CBC.
questions.a: Blood glucose, electrolytes, ECG and CBC

questions.question: A child with ulcerative colitis has fever, abdominal pain, toxicity and a dilated colon on X-ray. What is the management?
questions.exp: Colectomy if no improvement or perforation.
questions.b: IV steroids, IV antibiotics, bowel rest and urgent surgical review

questions.question: A 32-week preterm baby, 2 weeks old, becomes lethargic, refuses feeds and has abdominal distension. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pneumatosis on X-ray.

questions.question: A 2-month-old has a 1-day cough with wheeze and RR 55, after contact with his mother's cold. What is the management?
questions.exp: Palivizumab and RSV vaccines are preventive, not treatment.
questions.a: Supportive care with oxygen if hypoxic

questions.question: A child has recurrent left lower lobe infections and a lesion that does not fill with bronchographic dye while surrounding lung does. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sequestration does not communicate with the airway and is classic in the left lower lobe. The recall writer chose bronchogenic cyst.

questions.question: A 4-year-old has painless rectal bleeding, but episodes are preceded by severe abdominal pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pain before bleeding suggests intussusception (a Meckel diverticulum can be the lead point). Meckel bleeding is painless.

questions.question: A child has recurrent attacks of periumbilical pain with nausea and pallor, normal between attacks. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Functional.

questions.question: What is the empirical treatment of a brain abscess?
questions.exp: Cover streptococci, staphylococci and anaerobes.

questions.question: A 12-year-old has nephrotic syndrome with massive proteinuria and low albumin. What is the next step?
questions.exp: Over 10-12 years, minimal change is less likely, so biopsy is often done first. The recall writer chose methylprednisolone and listed biopsy as an option.

questions.question: A 2-year-old has dark urine, fever, constipation and BP 120/80, with urine WBC 10 and RBC 10, no protein. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Febrile UTI.

questions.question: What is the investigation for renal vein thrombosis?
questions.exp: Doppler.

questions.question: Below which platelet count is lumbar puncture relatively contraindicated?
questions.exp: Platelets < 50 (some use < 20-50) and coagulopathy increase bleeding risk.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of septic arthritis in children?
questions.exp: Kingella kingae is common under 4; Salmonella in sickle cell disease.

questions.question: A mixing study corrects a prolonged PTT. What does it suggest?
questions.exp: Correction means deficiency; no correction means inhibitor. Lupus anticoagulant is linked with thrombosis rather than bleeding.

questions.question: A 20-kg child in DKA is not shocked and has potassium 2.4 mmol/L. What is the fluid plan?
questions.exp: Correct hypokalaemia before insulin.
questions.a: 0.9% saline 10 mL/kg over 1 hour then deficit plus maintenance over 48 hours, with potassium added before insulin

questions.question: A 3-year-old with delayed walking and bowed legs has normal calcium, low phosphate, high PTH and ALP, and urinary phosphate reabsorption of 20%. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: High PTH drives phosphate wasting in vitamin D deficiency; XLH has normal PTH.

questions.question: Which test screens for Wilson disease?
questions.exp: Low ceruloplasmin and high 24-hour urinary copper.

questions.question: An 8-year-old girl is found on the ground unresponsive, not opening her eyes, with spontaneous breathing. What should be assessed?
questions.exp: Assess brainstem function.
